paragraphs: Children in care in Medway live with carers approved by Medway Council's own fostering service or by independent agencies such as the services shown above. The council's sufficiency strategy for 2026 to 2029, A place to call home, which went to its Cabinet in June 2026, counted 539 children in care at the end of December 2025, up from 458 in 2023, with about two in three of them living in foster homes.

Most of those foster homes are not the council's own. In December 2025, 85 children in care lived with Medway's own foster carers and 273 with independent or private carers, and the strategy reports that 62% of children in care were living outside Medway's local area. Around 64% are aged 10 to 17, and the strategy says the pressure for homes comes mainly from a growing group of 11 to 17-year-olds. It aims to grow the council's own pool of carers, with a focus on homes for children aged 10 and over.

The council's annual fostering report for 2025-26 gives the picture on 31 March 2026: 81 approved fostering households caring for 128 children, with 14 new households approved during the year from 212 enquiries, and an average of 7 months from enquiry to approval. The report says the gaps are clearest for older children, brothers and sisters, and children with more complex needs, and for 2026-27 the service aims to increase its approved households by 10%, with the focus on carers for teenagers, sibling groups and children with additional needs. Its eligibility rules have been revised so that applicants can combine fostering with work where that is appropriate.

Medway's carers are supported through supervision, training, peer support and the Mockingbird programme, which had three constellations supporting 21 fostering households and 33 children, with a fourth launched and two more planned. We do not yet have a Medway pay page, so ask the council for its current fees and allowances.

Fostering with the council means caring for Medway's own children close to home with its team behind you; an agency approves, trains and supports you itself, and councils, Medway among them, ask it to care for children who need a home. Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before you choose. If you live nearby, see our pages for Kent, Dartford and Bexley too.
